transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well, my wife actually suggested I come in. She thinks I've been too wound up lately. Which, you know, is fair, because grading has been an absolute nightmare this semester. I’m a teaching assistant—mostly handling the undergrad intro classes—and the sheer volume of essays... nobody knows how to use proper formatting anymore. I spent half my weekend just leaving comments about margins and citations. I actually had this one student who tried to cite a social media post as a primary academic source. Can you believe that? 

But anyway, the reason she wanted me to talk to someone is... well, I know my wife says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. She works in administration, so they're always changing protocols. Like last month, they completely overhauled the employee parking passes, which was a huge mess because they didn't send out the new stickers in time. 

But for the past year, her schedule and those little shifts in her messages... they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It's like there’s a private signal in them meant to tell me something she won’t say directly. I just wish people would communicate clearly, you know? Like with my students and their essays. Just tell me exactly what you mean instead of making me read between the lines.
Do you believe that people are sending you hidden messages or signals through their normal conversations or actions?

Well, exactly like I was just saying about my wife. I don't think it's strangers on the street or anything like that. But with her... yes. She keeps insisting that her late meetings and those weird little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. But it's been going on for the past year now, and they line up way too precisely to just be accidental. It really feels like there’s a private signal in them, meant to tell me something she won’t say directly. 

Which is ridiculous because it's not like we don't have the technology to just talk clearly. We pay for unlimited data. We actually switched our cell carrier to Verizon a couple of years ago because the coverage with AT&T was just abysmal in our neighborhood. We had this massive dead zone right by the kitchen island. You couldn't even pull up an email if you were standing too close to the refrigerator. I actually read an article about how certain older appliances can completely disrupt your home network frequencies. It makes you wonder what kind of radiation is leaking out of those things, honestly. Like the microwave in the TA lounge at the university—it has to be from the late nineties. It permanently smells like burnt popcorn because the freshmen don't understand how to use a simple wattage timer. I had to put a sticky note on the door of it last week just to explain that two minutes is too long for a snack-size bag.
Do you feel like anyone else, besides your wife, has also been sending you hidden messages or signals through their behavior or words?

No, no, it's really just my wife. I don't look at my students or the other TAs and think they're speaking in code or anything. Though, getting my students to communicate clearly about literally anything is a challenge in itself. 

Like, I was proctoring a midterm on Tuesday, and this one kid kept raising his hand to ask about the essay prompt. The prompt was literally just "Compare and contrast the main themes." It's not a trick question, but they overthink everything. And the lecture hall we were in was absolutely freezing, too. The HVAC system in the humanities building has been broken since October. They sent out an email saying maintenance was waiting on a specific part from Germany, which makes no sense to me because it's a standard commercial unit. I ended up having to wear my winter coat while grading papers in the back row. It’s one of those heavy wool peacoats, you know? Great for the wind when you're walking across campus, but terrible if you’re trying to sit comfortably in a tiny plastic chair for two hours. I actually had to take it to the dry cleaners last weekend because I spilled coffee on the cuff, and the prices they charge now are just outrageous.
Do you think your wife is deliberately trying to send you secret messages through her behavior and message changes, even if she denies it?

Well, yes, I do think that. I mean, I know my wife says the late meetings and little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but for the past year they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It really feels like there’s a private signal in them meant to tell me something she won’t say directly. 

Which is so frustrating because, like I said, we have the technology to communicate. We have cell phones. Though, speaking of phones, I actually had to go down to the Verizon store yesterday because my battery keeps draining by noon. The guy there—he couldn't have been older than twenty—tried to tell me I had too many background apps running. But I only use it for email, texts, and checking the weather. I don't even have any of those social media apps installed. I refuse to use them. The privacy policies are a nightmare. I read this whole article about how they track your location even when the app is closed. They sell the data to advertisers, which is why you'll be talking about, say, buying a new lawnmower, and suddenly you're getting ads for John Deere on every website you visit. Our lawnmower actually broke down last summer. The spark plug went bad, and I had to watch three different tutorial videos just to figure out how to replace it. The manual it came with was completely useless. It was translated from another language and half the diagrams were mislabeled. I ended up just having to guess which wrench to use.
Do you believe your wife’s behavior might be connected to some larger hidden plan or agenda, or do you think it’s just about trying to send you specific messages?

No, no, I don't think it's some grand conspiracy or a larger agenda. I really just think it's about her trying to send me specific messages about... well, whatever it is she feels she can't just say to my face. I mean, an agenda implies some big coordinated effort, like a department meeting. 

Which, speaking of agendas, the ones our department chair puts together are completely useless. We had a staff meeting on Thursday, and the agenda he emailed out was literally just three vague bullet points, but he still managed to talk for an hour and a half about administrative budget cuts. And the coffee they provide at those meetings is just dreadful. It's that cheap bulk powder stuff that comes in a massive plastic tub. I actually suggested to the committee that we should pool our money and buy one of those single-serve pod machines for the breakroom. I saw a really nice one on sale at Target over the weekend when I was looking for a new shower curtain. 

The plastic liner we have right now is getting that weird mildew at the bottom because the ventilation fan in our master bathroom sounds like a jet engine taking off, so my wife and I never turn it on. I tried taking the plastic cover off to clean the dust out of the motor a few weeks ago, but the screws were totally stripped. I couldn't get any grip on them at all. I swear, the contractor who built our house must have just used the cheapest hardware he could find at the discount supply store. It's the same story with the hinges on our kitchen cabinets, honestly.
Do you think the messages your wife is sending you are harmful, threatening, or have a negative intent behind them?

No, I don't think they're threatening or... or harmful, exactly. I don't feel like I'm in danger. It's more just... confusing. Like she's trying to tell me something about us, or maybe her job, but she just won't come out and say it. It's not malicious, it's just... exhausting trying to decode it all. 

Honestly, the most exhausting thing lately, though, has been trying to get my car inspected. I went down to the mechanic on Main Street—the one next to that old diner that closed down during the pandemic—and they told me I needed four new tires before they'd pass it. Four! I just bought the front two last spring. They tried to tell me the tread was wearing unevenly because my alignment was off, but the car drives perfectly straight. I think they just try to upsell you on everything. They had this whole display in the waiting room for premium windshield wipers that cost, like, sixty dollars a pair. Who pays sixty dollars for windshield wipers? You can get perfectly good ones at the auto parts store for fifteen bucks. I actually had to replace mine last month because the rubber started peeling off during that massive rainstorm we had. The one that flooded the underpass on Route 9? I got stuck in traffic for almost two hours because they had to detour everyone through the residential neighborhoods. People were driving on people's lawns to get around the barricades. It was absolute chaos.

Have you ever experienced any unusual thoughts, like hearing voices that others don’t hear, or believing things that most people would find very strange, outside of what you've already told me about your wife’s messages?

No, no voices or anything like that. I don't see things, I don't hear things. It's just the stuff with my wife that I mentioned. I mean, my mind is completely sound. I'm just a normal guy trying to figure out what's going on in my own house. 

Speaking of the house, though, I really need to clean the gutters this weekend. I was looking up at the roof yesterday when I was taking the trash out, and there's a literal sapling growing out of the corner downspout. It's ridiculous. The oak tree in our front yard drops so many leaves in the fall, and they just turn into this thick sludge over the winter. I usually hire this neighborhood kid to clean them out—he's the son of the couple who lives two doors down, the ones with the obnoxious wind chimes—but he went off to college in August. He's studying, I think, environmental science? Or maybe forestry. Something like that. His dad was telling me all about it when we were both at the hardware store a few weeks ago. I was there buying a new rake because the handle on my old wooden one finally snapped. I was raking up the pine needles in the backyard, and I guess I just pushed too hard, and the wood splintered right down the middle. I ended up getting one of those lightweight aluminum ones, but honestly, the grip on it is terrible. It gives me blisters if I use it for more than twenty minutes without gloves.
Do you ever feel like your understanding of your wife’s messages is something only you can see, and that others wouldn’t understand even if you explained it to them?

Yeah, exactly. That's the thing. I know my wife says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but... I mean, for the past year, they've lined up way too precisely to just be accidental. It's like there's a private signal in them meant to tell me something she won't say directly. And if I try to explain it to someone else, they just look at me like I'm reading too much into it. They don't see the pattern. 

Speaking of patterns, you should see the new tile my brother-in-law put in his kitchen. It's this intricate herringbone pattern, but whoever laid it completely messed up the grout lines near the refrigerator. It drives me crazy every time we go over there for dinner. We were just there on Sunday for a barbecue. He bought one of those massive ceramic egg smokers, and he spent literally fourteen hours smoking a brisket. Fourteen hours! I mean, it tasted fine, but I don't know who has that kind of time. I usually just throw some burgers on my gas grill and call it a day. Though, I do need to get my propane tank refilled. I went to use it last week, and the gauge was completely on empty. I usually go to the hardware store on 4th Street to get it swapped out, but the last time I was there, the guy working the register was so incredibly slow. He spent ten minutes trying to figure out how to scan a bag of potting soil for the lady in front of me. I almost just left the tank on the counter and walked out.
Do you think other people who know your wife well would also recognize these messages you describe, or do you think it's something only you can understand?

No, I don't think anyone else would get it. Her friends, her family... they just see her as this dedicated employee who works late. They don't know the way she phrases things when it's just the two of us, so they wouldn't catch the little shifts in her tone or the specific words she uses when she texts me about her schedule. It's meant for me. 

Speaking of schedules, my teaching assistant schedule this semester is a total nightmare. The professor I'm working for—Dr. Aris Thorne, he teaches this huge intro to macroeconomics lecture—he decided to move all his office hours to Thursday afternoons. Which means I have to grade literally two hundred quizzes by Friday morning every single week. I used to do my grading at this little coffee shop near the campus library, the one with the really good blueberry scones? But they just changed their Wi-Fi policy, and now you can only get an hour of internet with a purchase. An hour! How am I supposed to grade two hundred quizzes in an hour? I ended up having to buy three separate coffees last week just to stay online. By the time I left, I had the worst caffeine jitters. I was shaking so bad I could barely get my key in the ignition of my car. And of course, that was the day it decided to snow, just a dusting, but enough to make the roads slick. People around here completely forget how to drive the second a single snowflake falls. I saw a guy in a giant pickup truck slide right through a red light on College Avenue. Didn't even tap his brakes. It's a miracle he didn't T-bone anyone.
Do you think your interpretation of your wife’s behavior is the only correct one, or do you think others might reasonably see it differently?

Well, I mean, I guess someone else might look at it and say, sure, maybe she's just busy, but... they don't know her like I do. Like I said before, she claims the late meetings and those weird little shifts in how she writes her texts are just normal office stuff. But I've been tracking this for the past year, and they just line up way too perfectly to be an accident. It's obvious to me that there's a private signal in there, something she's trying to communicate without saying it out loud. 

Speaking of communicating, my car insurance company has been sending me these endless emails about switching to paperless billing. They email me like three times a week. I finally called them to make it stop, and I was on hold for forty-five minutes. Forty-five minutes! Just listening to this terrible elevator music, like a saxophone cover of some 80s pop song. I think it was Hall and Oates? Anyway, when I finally got a real person, it was this guy who sounded like he was eating a sandwich while he was talking to me. I could literally hear him chewing. It was so unprofessional. I almost asked to speak to his supervisor, but honestly, I just wanted to get off the phone so I could go pick up my dry cleaning. I use this place on Elm Street, and they do a great job with my shirts, but the parking lot is a nightmare. It's shared with a bakery, and people just abandon their cars anywhere to run in and get a croissant. I had to park two blocks away last time and carry five heavy shirts in the rain.
Even though others may offer different explanations for your wife’s behavior, do you feel certain that your interpretation is the only correct one?

Yeah, I am certain. I mean, I know she keeps telling me it's just normal office stuff, the late meetings, the way her texts change... but like I said, for a whole year now, it's just too precise. It can't be an accident. It's a private signal, and I know I'm right about it. 

Just like I knew I was right about the thermostat in my apartment. My landlord tried to tell me it was working fine, but I knew it was running at least three degrees colder than what the dial said. I finally bought a digital thermometer just to prove it to him. I had to go to three different stores to find one that wasn't overly complicated. I ended up at that big box store out by the highway, the one with the massive parking lot where they always have the garden center taking up half the space in the spring? Well, they had all the Christmas stuff out already, and it was only October. I mean, who is buying artificial trees in October? It's ridiculous. I had to navigate through a maze of inflatable Santas just to find the hardware aisle. And then, when I finally got the thermometer and showed my landlord, he still tried to argue with me about the placement of the sensor. Some people just refuse to see what's right in front of them, you know?
Even though others may offer different explanations for your wife’s behavior, do you feel certain that your interpretation is the only correct one?

I know you keep asking me this, and I know I already said it, but yes, I'm absolutely certain. I know my wife says the late meetings and those little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but I've been watching this for a year. For the past year, they've lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It's like there's a private signal in them meant to tell me something she won't say directly. I just know it. 

Speaking of things lining up, I was trying to align the shelves in my living room yesterday. I bought these floating shelves from IKEA—well, not IKEA, it was actually Wayfair, because the IKEA shipping costs are just outrageous right now. Have you seen how much they charge just to deliver a flat-pack box? It's absurd. Anyway, I got these shelves to display my collection of vintage cameras. I have this beautiful 1970s Canon AE-1, the one with the silver body? It's a classic. I picked it up at a flea market last summer. The guy selling it didn't even know what he had, he just had it sitting in a cardboard box next to some rusty tools. I had to haggle with him for twenty minutes because he suddenly decided it was a "family heirloom" the second I showed interest. People do that, you know? They try to inflate the value of things just because you're looking at them. But I got the shelves up, and I had to use a laser level because the floor in my apartment is slightly slanted. If you drop a marble in the kitchen, it rolls all the way into the hallway. It drives me crazy when things aren't perfectly straight.
Even though others may offer different explanations for your wife’s behavior, do you feel certain that your interpretation is the only correct one?

Look, I... I feel like we're going in circles here, Doc. Yes, I am one hundred percent certain. I know she says the late meetings and the weird little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but I've been watching this for a year. For the past year, they've lined up way too precisely to be an accident. It's a private signal, meant to tell me something she won't just come out and say directly. I know I'm right about this. 

Just like I knew I was right about the tires on my car. I took it in for an oil change last week, just to that quick-lube place down the street, and the mechanic tried to tell me I needed four brand new tires. Said the tread was dangerously low. But I just bought those tires two years ago! I drive a 2015 Honda Civic, I'm not out there drag racing or off-roading. I mostly just drive to the university and back. The parking at the university is a whole other story, though. I have a staff pass, but the designated lot is always full by 8:00 AM because they let the undergrads park there if they pay a premium. It's ridiculous. I'm a teaching assistant, I have actual classes to prep for, and I end up having to park in the visitor structure and walk half a mile across campus in the freezing cold. I complained to the parking authority, but they just sent me this automated email response. It's like no one actually listens anymore, you know? They just want to sell you things you don't need, like those tires. I ended up taking my car to a different shop, a local guy my neighbor recommended, and he said the tires were perfectly fine for at least another ten thousand miles. See? You just have to trust your own judgment.
Even when people offer logical explanations or evidence that contradicts your interpretation of your wife’s behavior, do you still believe your understanding is the only correct one?

Yes, I do. I mean, look, I hear what people are saying, and I know my wife keeps telling me the late meetings and those weird little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. But I've been watching this for a year now. For the past twelve months, they've just lined up way too precisely to feel accidental. It's like there's a private signal in them, you know? Something meant to tell me what she won't just say directly. 

It reminds me of when I was trying to get the university to fix the projector in my seminar room. I told them for weeks that the color balance was off—everything had this faint green tint to it. It drove me crazy. I was trying to show these slides on medieval architecture, and the cathedrals looked like they were covered in moss. I put in three different maintenance requests, and every time, they sent back an email saying it was "within normal operating parameters." Normal operating parameters! Can you believe that? It's just like the parking situation I mentioned before. The bureaucracy at that school is stifling. They have this whole new online portal for faculty requests, and it's supposedly designed to streamline things, but really it just creates this wall between you and the actual people who can fix the problem. You submit a ticket, and it just vanishes into the ether. I finally had to track down the head of the AV department while he was getting coffee at the student union just to get someone to actually look at the projector. And you know what? I was right. The bulb was failing. You just can't always trust the official explanation people give you.
Even when people offer logical explanations or evidence that contradicts your interpretation of your wife’s behavior, do you still believe your understanding is the only correct one?

Doc, is this... are you testing my memory or something? Because I really feel like a broken record here. But yes, my answer is still exactly the same. I don't care what "logical" explanations people try to hand me. My wife swears up and down that her late meetings and those specific little changes in her work messages are just regular office stuff. But I've been tracking this for a year now. A whole year. The way they line up is just way too precise to be some random accident. It's a private signal. It's her way of telling me something without actually having the guts to say it out loud. 

Speaking of people not having the guts to be honest, you should see the essays I've been grading this week. I had this one undergrad—Intro to Sociology—who turned in a ten-page paper that was so obviously written by one of those AI chatbots. I mean, it used the words "rich tapestry" and "delve" in almost every single paragraph. Nineteen-year-olds do not write like that. I brought it to the professor I assist, and he just rubbed his temples and told me we don't have a strict enough university policy yet to prove it, so we just have to grade it on the rubric. Just let it slide! Can you believe that? We're supposed to be an academic institution. If we don't uphold basic standards of integrity, the whole system just collapses. 

I actually had to start drinking chamomile tea while I grade just to keep my blood pressure from spiking. My sister sent me this expensive loose-leaf blend from Arizona. She moved out to Sedona a few years ago and got really into all that new-age holistic stuff. She keeps trying to mail me amethyst geodes to "clear my apartment's energy," which is honestly just a nightmare for dusting. Do you know how hard it is to get dust out of the crevices of a geode? You basically need a can of compressed air, like the kind you use for computer keyboards. I used to have a really nice mechanical keyboard, actually, the kind with the loud clicky switches... wait, what were we talking about again?
